<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:spencer} For any real symmetric matrices $A_{1},\ldots,A_{d}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$
with $\lVertA_{i}\rVert\le1$, there are signs $\varepsilon_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_{d}\in\{-1,1\}$
satisfying $
\lVert\sum^{d}_{i=1}\varepsilon_{i}A_{i}\rVert\lesssim d^{1/2}$.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:F'(t)} For $0<t\le1$, we have $-F'(t)=\frac{2}{t}\,\{b\operatorname{Tr}(\mathbb{E}_{\mu_{t}}[X^{2}_{t}])+\alpha\operatorname{Tr}(\mathbb{E}_{\mu_{t}}[X^{4}_{t}(I-X_t)^{-1}])\}$, where
\[\mathrm{d}\mu_{t}(g)=\frac{1}{Z_{t}}\,e^{-V(X_{t}(g))}\,\mathrm{d}\gamma_{n}(g)\,.\]
As $V$ is convex, $\mu_t$ is a log-concave tilt of the Gaussian. Moreover as $V$ is even, so is $\mu_t$.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By differentiation,
\[
-F'(t)=-\frac{Z'_{t}}{Z_{t}}=\frac{1}{Z_{t}}\,\mathbb{E}_{\gamma_{n}}[\partial_{t}V(X_{t})\cdot e^{-V(X_{t})}]=\mathbb{E}_{\mu_{t}}\partial_{t}V(X_{t})\,.
\]
Using $X_{t}=tX$ and $\mathrm{d}(\log \det A(t)) = \operatorname{Tr} (A(t)^{-1}  \,\mathrm{d} A(t))$, a simple calculation gives
\[
\partial_{t}V(X_{t})=\frac{2}{t}\,\bigl[b\operatorname{Tr} X^{2}_{t}+\alpha\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(X^{4}_{t}\,(I-X^{2}_{t})^{-1}\bigr)\bigr]\,.
\]
The expectation $\mathbb{E}_{\mu_t}\partial_{t}V(X_{t})$ can be simplified further. As $(I-X^{2}_{t})^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\,[(I-X_{t})^{-1}+(I+X_{t})^{-1}]$, and as $\mu_{t}$ is even, $(I-X_t)^{-1}$ and $(I+X_t)^{-1}$ have the same distribution. Hence, one has
\[
\mathbb{E}_{\mu_t}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(X^4_{t}\,(I-X^{2}_t)^{-1}\bigr) = 
\mathbb{E}_{\mu_t} \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(X^{4}_{t}\,(I-X_{t})^{-1}\bigr)\,,\]
which gives the claimed expression for $-F'(t)$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:moments}
 For $0\le t\le1$, we have:\vspace{-8pt}
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item (Second moment bound.) $\mathbb{E}_{\mu_t} X_t^2 \preceq S_t-I \preceq 8 \eta t^2 I$, and hence  $\mathbb{E}_{\mu_t} \operatorname{Tr}(X_t^2) \leq 8 \eta t^2 d$.  
     \item (Fourth moment bound.) $\mathbb{E}_{\mu_t}\operatorname{Tr}(X_t^4R_t) \le 128 \eta^2  t^4 d$.
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:identity} 
$XRX=R-I-X$ and thus $\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[XRX] = S-I$. Moreover, $\mathbb{E}_\mu X^2 \preceq \mathbb{E}_\mu XRX$.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
As $R\,(I-X)=I$ by definition, we have 
$RX=XR=R-I$. Using this again gives  $X^2R= X (R-I) = R-I-X$.
Taking expectation and using $\mathbb{E}_{\mu}X=0$, gives $S-I=\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[XRX]$.

For the second part, using $R = I+X+ X^2 +\cdots $, multiplying by $X$ on both sides, and taking expectations gives $\mathbb{E}_\mu[XRX]=\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[\sum_{k\geq 1}X^{2k}]\succeq \mathbb{E}_{\mu}[X^{2}]$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
We now prove Lemma \ref{lem:moments}.
By Lemma \ref{lem:identity}, we need to bound $\mathbb{E}_\mu \operatorname{Tr} (X^2R)$ and $\mathbb{E}_\mu \operatorname{Tr} (X^4 R)$.
The key tool will be the matrix Brascamp--Lieb (BL) inequality~\cite{CorderoErausquin18,AkbasSra26}. 
It says the following.
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
For $f_a = X^2 z_a$, the derivative is $\partial_{i}f_{a}=\frac{t}{r}\,(A_{i}X+XA_{i})\,z_{a}$.
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:matrix-poincare} Suppose that $\mathcal{K}_{M}\succeq\kappa G$
on convex $\Omega$ for some $\kappa>0$. Then, every $C^{1}$ function
$f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with $\int_{\Omega}f^{\mathsf{T}}Mf\,\mathrm{d} g<\infty$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Var}_{M}f\le\frac{1}{\kappa}\int_{\Omega}\lVert\nabla f\rVert^{2}_{G}\,\mathrm{d} g=\frac{1}{\kappa}\int\sum^{n}_{i=1}(\partial_{i}f)^{\mathsf{T}}M\,(\partial_{i}f)\,\mathrm{d} g\,.\label{eq:matrix-poincare}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lem-4 -->
